Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

titleclassifier (development version)

Baseline performance

This is the first entry in the changelog. It records where the package stands so that later changes can be measured against it. All numbers come from the validation scripts in data-raw/partvii-validation/, run on the NCCS efile tables (release efile_v2_3), and are reported in full in the Performance article (vignettes/articles/performance.Rmd).

  • Coverage. On the 2019-2023 calibration sample (60,520 filings, 699,276 title rows), weighted to the population, 96.1% of title rows reach a standard title (95.3% by exact crosswalk match, 0.8% by pattern rule) and 3.7% remain uncoded. Every person still gets a role, because step 09 resolves uncoded titles from the checkboxes, pay and hours.
  • Accuracy on the hand-labeled set (312 people on 2010-2012 filings): 90.4% get the right role (990: 90.1%; 990-EZ: 92.5%). Recall by labeled role: CEO 100%, DUAL 100%, PROFESSIONAL 95.0%, BOARD 94.0%, OFFICER 70.8%, MANAGER 64.3%, STAFF 58.3%. Unpaid people get the right role 97.7% of the time and paid people 87.5%. Of the board members identified correctly, 98.2% also get the right board role.
  • 990-EZ returns (no checkboxes, so step 09 uses a model). On held-out form switchers with the same title in both years (10,558 people), the model agrees with the full-990-year role 96.7% of the time (rules: 95.1%), and 74.0% for people not on the board (rules: 63.6%).
  • Chief executive. On the CEO label set (750 filings from 150 organizations), step 09 names the right chief executive for 88.1% of filings and gives board seats the right board role 98.7% of the time. On the held-out set (126 filings from 64 other organizations) it names the right chief executive for 81.7%.
  • Stability over time. For the 6,000 organizations followed from 2019 to 2023, 95-98% of people keep their role from one year to the next (board members: 99.2%), and in most groups 88-92% of organizations keep the same CEO.

Name parsing for the validation scripts: peopleparser 0.2.0

Name parsing is not part of the package pipeline. Only the scripts that link people across years, 15-panel-synthid.R and 18-switch-labels.R, parse names, using peopleparser before synthid::link_panel().

  • peopleparser is now a declared dependency: peopleparser (>= 0.2.0) in Suggests, installed from the v0.2.0 tag through Remotes. Both scripts stop with the install command if an older version is installed.
  • Both scripts call parse_names(add_nicknames = TRUE) and carry the new first-name variant columns (first_name_type, first_name_formal, first_name_nicknames, first_name_canonical, canonical_rule) into their linked output. synthid already matches nicknames using the same variant table, so the links themselves do not change.
  • Since peopleparser 0.2.0, parse_names() no longer starts its own parallel workers. Both scripts now pass workers = NW, so parsing still uses the script’s worker count (all cores but one by default).
  • Rerunning either script with peopleparser 0.2.0 can change a few parses, and so a few links, compared with earlier outputs. The main causes are the 2020 Census name tables, more credential stripping, and two-word names keeping their written order. On peopleparser’s own sample of 9,608 Part VII names, 0.1.0 changed 253 first or last names and 0.2.0 changed 20 more. The baseline numbers above were produced before this update.
